newsitem.title: USA: Mass Gov seeks to cut unemployment insurance costs.
newsitem.headline: Mass Gov seeks to cut unemployment insurance costs.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld said Thursday he submitted a bill to reduce employers' contributions to the Unemployment Insurance fund, saving business $90 million in 1997 alone.

"Business is booming, unemployment is at record lows and workers compensation rates continue to plummet. The time is ripe to lower the guillotine on unemployment insurance rates," said Weld in prepared remarks.

The governor said the reductions were needed to make the state more competitive, as its high unemployment insurance costs are second only to Rhode Island. The proposed cuts would bring Massachusetts' rates, now two-and-a-half times the national median, closer in line with competing states.
Massachusetts employers now pay an average of $468 per employee each year, and the new bill would cut the so-called Schedule D rate to a Schedule C rate, saving firms $50 per employee.
Even with the proposed rate cut, the Unemployment Insurance Fund, which was near bankruptcy in 1991, was projected to reach what Weld called a "healthy balance" of over $1 billion by year-end.

Unless the legislature approves the reductions this year, however, Weld warned that the Schedule D rates automatically will jump even higher to Schedule E rates. He did not disclose how big the rise would be.
